text: So, the Moon vanishes. What happens in the very first second? Well, moonlight takes just over a second to reach us. So for one more second, you'd still see it. Then, the sky is empty. Earth and the Moon actually swing around a shared balance point, about four thousand seven hundred kilometres from Earth's centre. Without the Moon, that monthly wobble simply stops. Earth keeps circling the Sun almost exactly as before. No crash, and nobody flies off into space.
